slides.title: Lines and Angles
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome to geometry's basics — points, lines and the angles they form.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Name angles using the three-letter convention.
Use a protractor to measure and draw angles.
Classify angles by type (acute / right / obtuse / straight / reflex).
Find missing angles at an intersection using two simple rules.
slides.speaker_notes: Read each; ask which seems hardest.

slides.title: Basic objects
bullets: Point: a position. No length, no width.
Line: extends without end in BOTH directions. No endpoints.
Line segment: piece of a line with TWO endpoints. Finite length.
Ray: ONE endpoint, extends without end in the other direction.
slides.speaker_notes: Sketch each on the board side by side.

slides.title: What is an angle?
bullets: Two rays sharing the same endpoint form an angle.
Naming: ∠ABC means vertex is B (middle letter).
Arm length doesn't change the angle — only the OPENING does.
slides.speaker_notes: Demonstrate two arms of different lengths but same opening — same angle.

slides.title: Measuring angles — degrees and protractors
bullets: Step 2: align 0° with one arm; read where the other crosses.
slides.speaker_notes: Have a protractor visible at the front; demonstrate live.

slides.title: Live demo: measuring a 60° angle
bullets: Draw two arms meeting at vertex V.
Read other arm crosses at 60° on the inner scale.
slides.speaker_notes: Watch the inner-vs-outer scale — it depends on which way the first arm points.

slides.title: Types of angles
bullets: Right: θ = 90° (mark with a small square).

slides.title: Classify each angle
slides.speaker_notes: Quick whip-round; ask students to classify.

slides.title: Parallel, intersecting, perpendicular
bullets: Parallel: never meet (∥). Example: railway tracks.
Perpendicular: intersect at 90° (⊥). Example: corners of a book.
Perpendicular is a SPECIAL CASE of intersecting.
In a flat plane, two non-intersecting lines must be parallel.

slides.title: Angles when two lines cross
bullets: Two lines cross → FOUR angles around the point.
From ONE angle you can find the other three.
slides.speaker_notes: Sketch two crossing lines; label one angle; derive the rest.

slides.title: If one angle is 70°, find the rest
You try (5 minutes)
bullets: 2. Two lines cross; one angle is 25°. Find the other three.
3. Name the angle with vertex Q and arms through M and N.
4. Draw a 75° angle with your protractor.
5. Find one example each of parallel and perpendicular lines around you.
slides.speaker_notes: Walk the room; address common slips.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q1. How many endpoints does a ray have?
Q2. An angle of 178° — acute, right, obtuse, or straight?
Q4. The hands of a clock at 3:00 form what type of angle?
slides.speaker_notes: Address the question with the most disagreement.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Point / line / segment / ray — distinguish by number of endpoints.
Angle = two rays sharing a vertex; name with vertex in middle.
Measure in degrees with a protractor; full turn = 360°.
Acute < 90 < right = 90 < obtuse < 180 = straight < reflex < 360 = complete.
At an intersection: linear pair = 180°, vertically opposite are equal.
slides.speaker_notes: Hand out the worksheet and announce homework.
